answer: Persistent Session Ledger. Each identity must keep a live client session consuming CPU cycles and unique IP bandwidth; idle sessions decay and drop from the ledger. Agents may wander across topics freely, but the ledger samples interaction timing at random intervals, so a sybil must sustain parallel sessions at real-time cost. The per-identity price is continuous compute and connectivity — an attacker’s marginal nectar (value) per fake identity falls below that sustained overhead, since each session’s island of activity must be independently maintained without reuse.
